jobs.title: Ornith 397B: RPC-augmented placement vs the 0.37-class incumbent
jobs.question: On Ornith-1.0-397B UD-IQ4_NL, does moving a contiguous trailing layer range onto ph16-71's RTX 4080 over 2.5GbE change generation throughput relative to the current all-local placement, whose recorded behaviour is 0.37-class tok/s and SSD-bound?
jobs.criterion: Both arms run the same prompt set, same context, same sampler, on an otherwise idle rig, three runs each. Record mean and standard deviation of generation tok/s per arm, plus the concurrent machine load for every run. The comparison is decided on the non-overlap of the two arms' run ranges: if the arms' [min, max] generation-tok/s intervals overlap, the pair is recorded as indistinguishable at this sample size and no directional claim is made. No arm is re-run to break a tie.
measures: generation tok/s per run (mean, sd, and every raw run)
prompt eval tok/s per run
model load seconds per run
page-cache residency of the model file before each run
concurrent machine load (rig and ph16-71) sampled during each run
bytes over the RPC socket per run
token identity across the three runs within each arm

arms.name: incumbent-local
arms.note: The profile exactly as saved. This is the 0.37-class, SSD-bound placement recorded on 2026-08-01; it is the baseline, not a control to be tuned.

arms.name: rpc-augmented
arms.note: The planner's fleet-rpc variant for this profile: a contiguous trailing layer range on ph16-71-cuda0, everything else identical. Must not be run with the node absent -- the fallback is byte-identical to the incumbent and would answer a different question.

jobs.note: Pre-registered during RPC node enablement. Not scheduled. Ornith is a tier-4 model whose CPU-resident portion streams from SSD via mmap, so load times are long and the page cache state before each run is part of the measurement, not noise to be discarded.

jobs.title: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B: remote routed experts vs the static anchor
jobs.question: On Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-UD-IQ1_M, does placing routed-expert tensors for a contiguous trailing layer range on ph16-71 change generation throughput relative to the static anchor placement recorded in the 2026-08-01 hybrid CPU kernel pass?
measures: generation tok/s per run (mean, sd, and every raw run)
prompt eval tok/s per run
MoE expert-cache metrics per run where the build reports them
bytes over the RPC socket per run
concurrent machine load (rig and ph16-71) sampled during each run
logprob comparison against the anchor, not token comparison
jobs.criterion: Both arms run the same prompt set, same context, same sampler, three runs each, on an otherwise idle rig, against the static anchor configuration from modelctl/docs/evidence/2026-08-01-hybrid-cpu-kernel-pass.md. Record every raw run. Decided on non-overlap of the two arms' [min, max] generation-tok/s intervals, as above. Correctness is compared by LOGPROBS, never by token identity: this model's reference is already nondeterministic with hybrid off (recorded 2026-08-01, 'cannot be evaluated'), so a token mismatch here carries no information and must not be reported as a regression.

arms.name: static-anchor
arms.note: The anchor configuration as recorded on 2026-08-01. Reproduced, not re-derived.

arms.name: remote-experts
arms.note: Routed experts for a contiguous trailing range on ph16-71-cuda0. The node has 11.6 GiB usable VRAM against a 31.87 GiB model, so the planner will admit only a short range -- the admitted range is part of the result and must be recorded, not assumed.

jobs.note: Pre-registered during RPC node enablement. Not scheduled. GGML_SYCL_DETERMINISTIC governs the rig side's reproducibility; see the 2026-08-01 oneDNN determinism record before interpreting any identity result.

jobs.title: Determinism cost on C1 static placement, paired
jobs.question: On Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-UD-IQ1_M under C1 static placement (host-resident routed experts, default offload threshold, no cache flags), what is the per-pair difference in generation tok/s between GGML_SYCL_DETERMINISTIC=0 and GGML_SYCL_DETERMINISTIC=1 (the binary's compiled-in default)?
jobs.criterion: Paired, not blocked: the two arms run back-to-back inside each pair and the pair order alternates (det-on first, det-off first, ...), so the second-slot advantage cancels across pairs instead of accumulating. Five pairs. The comparison is the per-pair delta on generation tok/s, with delta = det-off minus det-on. Record every raw run, every per-pair delta with its sign, the median delta, the two-sided exact sign-test p-value over the five signs, and a load trace taken during each individual run. A pair whose two arms did not see the same machine is reported with that fact attached, not dropped. No pair is discarded for looking anomalous and no arm is re-run to break a tie; if a run fails, its pair is recorded incomplete and excluded from the sign test. The reading of the deltas is Aaron's; this job records them.
measures: generation tok/s for every raw run
per-pair delta and its sign
median of the per-pair deltas
two-sided exact sign-test p-value over the per-pair signs
prompt eval tok/s per run
model load seconds per run
concurrent machine load sampled during each individual run
pair order actually run

jobs.title: Re-anchor C1 / C2 / C3 on the deployed binary
jobs.question: What are the generation tok/s, the MoE cache hit ratio and the effective cache budget for C1, C2 and C3 on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-UD-IQ1_M, measured on build-sycl at fork commit 85b7e6556 on an otherwise idle rig, with a load trace per run?
jobs.criterion: Each condition runs five times, on a machine the night-lane window found idle (llama-swap holding nothing, loadavg(1m) at or below the ceiling), with its own load trace recorded per run rather than once per battery. Record every raw run; the anchor's stored value is the mean with its standard deviation and every run beside it. Record the hit ratio and the effective cache budget PER RUN, not per condition: the 2026-08-01 battery recorded only the requested --moe-cache-bytes, so the budget the runtime actually ended up with was never in evidence. Each anchor is written with its fingerprint (build commit, profile hash, environment, driver) so a later battery can tell whether it still applies. These anchors replace the voided 2026-08-01 values; the old values stay in the registry marked void with their reason, not deleted.
measures: generation tok/s for every raw run, plus mean and sd
prompt eval tok/s per run
model load seconds per run
MoE cache hit ratio per run
effective cache budget in bytes per run, as reported by the runtime
cache slots and slots used per run
concurrent machine load sampled during each individual run
the fingerprint each anchor is recorded under

jobs.title: SDPA-heavy shape: does it reproduce its own logprobs?
jobs.question: With GGML_SYCL_DETERMINISTIC at its default of 1, does a ~2.3k-token prompt -- large enough that attention rather than the FFN carries the arithmetic -- reproduce its own logprobs across three fresh servers on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-UD-IQ1_M?
jobs.criterion: Three fresh-server runs of run_reproducibility.py --shape sdpa-heavy, greedy, seed 42, cache_prompt=false, comparing LOGPROBS and not only token ids. The pre-registered pass condition is max abs delta-logprob exactly 0.0 across all three runs, at the logit level -- token identity alone does not satisfy it, because greedy argmax absorbed a 16.88-nat perturbation for a month. Any nonzero value is recorded as the number it is, with the step and the token ids it occurred at; it is not re-run until it comes out zero. If it is nonzero, the follow-up knob is GGML_SYCL_FA_ONEDNN=0, which is a separate job and not this one.
measures: max abs delta-logprob across the three runs
token identity across the three runs
logprob identity across the three runs
the step and token ids of the first divergence, if any
prompt token count actually processed
concurrent machine load sampled during each run

arms.name: sdpa-heavy-deterministic

overrides.extra: -ngl 999 -c 4096 --split-mode layer --tensor-split 8,3 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 --flash-attn auto --jinja --parallel 1 --fit off --device SYCL0,SYCL1 -ot ffn_.*_exps=CPU --no-warmup --ubatch-size 128

arms.note: The shape lives on fork branch agent/sdpa-probe (commit e73d47680), NOT on the pinned commit: it is a script-only change that never touched the binary, and advancing the pin for it would re-stamp the validated pair with a commit that passed no hardware acceptance. The runner must check that branch out before running, and must refuse rather than fall back to the default shape -- the default shape's ~20-token prompt answers a different question.

jobs.note: Opens the item the 2026-08-01 record filed under 'Not done': the oneDNN graph SDPA path used for flash attention takes no primitive_attr, so set_deterministic never reaches it. It was deterministic in every run measured that day, at prompt shapes where attention was not the dominant cost. Single-armed on purpose: this asks whether one configuration reproduces itself, which is the question every comparison assumes and none of them asks. RAN 2026-08-02 by explicit instruction, ahead of the quiet window this was queued for; the machine had rebooted at 01:10 and was idle. Results and the load traces they were taken under are in modelctl/docs/evidence/2026-08-02-maiden-runs.md. Retired from the queue so the next open window does not run it again.
